How many chiro sessions will I need? The honest answer is "it depends", and Mr Turtle wanted to know on what.

How long it's been going on, how much it affects your day, and your sleep, stress and activity levels all shape the plan. A recent niggle often improves within a handful of visits. Longer-standing pain usually shifts towards exercise and daily habits, with visits spreading out.

caption:
Painted the ceiling, then hung the Christmas lights. Now Lulu's neck won't turn 🎄

Looking up for long periods holds the neck tipped back while your shoulders work above head height. It's usually the combination and the time, not the task itself, that leaves things sore.

Get closer to the job with a stable ladder, work in 10 to 15 minute blocks with a break looking straight ahead, and swap hands on the roller or drill. Afterwards, gentle chin nods and shoulder rolls. Most soreness settles within a few days with movement.

Arm tingling, dizziness looking up, building headaches or any fall from a ladder are worth getting checked. Our Chatswood and Sydney CBD physios can help. Book online via the link in bio.

caption:
Kneeling, lifting, reaching overhead and twisting in tight spaces. For a tradie like Lulu, your body is the main tool.

Most niggles come from repeating the same thing without enough capacity for it. Gym machines train neat, stable movements; Pilates trains control through odd angles, like lifting from a twist or holding a half squat under a sink. When the hips and mid-back move well, the lower back does less of the twisting.

Before site: ten slow bridges, ten side-lying leg lifts each side and a few open books. One or two Pilates sessions a week is a realistic start.

Leg numbness or weakness, or pain after a fall, is worth assessing first. Our Pilates team at Hybrid Physio can help. Book online via the link in bio.

caption:
Stretching every day and the hamstrings still feel tight? Toto's been there.

Hamstrings can feel tight because they're tired, protective or underloaded, not only because they lack length. That's why stretching alone often doesn't change the feeling for long.

Remedial massage can help them feel easier in the short term, and that's a useful window for movement. Add a gentle supported stretch for about 30 seconds, then bridges and Romanian deadlifts twice a week. Massage complements strength work; it doesn't replace it.

Tingling, pain down the leg or low back pain alongside it are worth a physio or GP assessment. Our remedial massage therapists at Hybrid Physio can help. Book online via the link in bio.

Warmth before a remedial massage, like a warm shower or heat pack, often helps tight muscles relax so the session feels easier. Afterwards, go with what feels good. Most people just enjoy a warm shower, and ice usually isn't needed.

caption:
Carriage, springs, footbar... is the reformer speaking a different language?

The carriage is the sliding platform you lie or kneel on. Springs add resistance, but heavier springs can actually make some moves easier by giving you support, while lighter ones ask for more control. The footbar is your base for pushing, and the straps link your hands or feet to the springs for pulling.

Knowing the terms makes cues easier to follow, so you can focus on moving well instead of wondering what two reds and a blue means. Always check the carriage is still before climbing on or off.
